title: Allahabad HC Quashes 1999 Dismissal of PNB Employee Over Missing Inquiry Record
case_name: P.K. Nigam v. Punjab National Bank and Others
citation: WRIT - A No. 58 of 2000, decided 26 October 2026
card_summary: The Allahabad High Court, Lucknow Bench, quashed a 1999 order dismissing a Punjab National Bank employee after a disciplinary inquiry held between 1997 and 1999. The court had earlier directed the bank to produce the original inquiry record, and the bank could not, citing a misplaced file. Without that record the bank could not show the inquiry had given the employee a fair hearing, so the dismissal could not stand.
card_tip: A bank or any employer that relies on a disciplinary inquiry to justify dismissal must preserve the original inquiry record; its loss years later can unravel the dismissal regardless of the underlying misconduct.
verification_notes: Decision date and core facts (1999 dismissal, 1997-99 inquiry, bank's failure to produce the original record despite a prior court direction) confirmed by both LiveLaw and SupremeToday. Reports differ on the precise relief granted (service restoration versus limiting the ruling to the legality of the disciplinary action), so the card states only the quashing of the dismissal, which both sources agree on. Full judgment text not independently read.
